_meta.role: Deep Learning Computer Architect - New College Grad 2026

summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology with hands-on experience in CUDA kernel parallelization and optimization, LLM performance tuning, and GPU memory hierarchy analysis. Parallelized VGG16 conv layers with custom CUDA C++ kernels (1.5–2× speedup), implemented Q/K/V projections and multi-head self-attention from first principles in PyTorch, and benchmarked four MPI parallelization strategies achieving 30× speedup — characterizing load balance and scalability trade-offs across each approach.

experience.title: Research Fellowship
bullets: Trained U-Net segmentation with VGG-16, VGG-19, and ResNet-50 backbones on BraTS 2020; characterized accuracy-latency trade-offs across backbone architectures using Dice Score and IoU; led a cross-cultural team of 7 to deliver the full pipeline within a 6-week window.

experience.title: AI/ML Intern
bullets: Fine-tuned DONUT transformer on a custom dataset in PyTorch; improved validation accuracy from 55% to 93% via targeted preprocessing, standardized training pipelines, and model tuning.

experience.title: Deep Learning Intern
bullets: Trained YOLOv8 on a custom toothbrush detection dataset for health-level classification; improved accuracy from 78% to 97.5% through dataset curation, annotation, and model tuning.
Evaluated model performance end-to-end and deployed in a consumer mobile app.

projects.name: CUDA Kernel Optimization for VGG16 Inference
bullets: Parallelized all 13 VGG16 Conv2D layers using the LibTorch C++ API with custom CUDA C++ kernels; profiled each layer via cudaEvent_t; optimized global memory access via coalescing, constant memory for weights, and preallocated buffers to eliminate per-layer allocation overhead.

Achieved ~35% speedup (49.2ms vs. 73.3ms uncoalesced, 77.5ms CPU TorchScript); identified global memory bandwidth as the primary bottleneck in the uncoalesced baseline and resolved it through memory hierarchy optimizations — 1.5–2× throughput gain at identical accuracy.

projects.name: GPT-2 Style Language Model from Scratch
bullets: Implemented a GPT-2-style Transformer in PyTorch from scratch: multi-head self-attention, MLP blocks, residual connections, layer norm, and weight tying.

Built a TikToken-based tokenizer and training loop with perplexity evaluation; implemented Q/K/V projections, scaled dot-product attention, and feed-forward blocks from first principles, applying theoretical study of Transformer internals from prior LLM compression work.

projects.name: SLM Compression and Benchmarking for Edge Deployment
bullets: Applied structured pruning and 8-bit quantization to TinyLlama 1.1B in PyTorch as LLM performance tuning techniques; reduced memory footprint by ~25% and benchmarked task accuracy across HellaSwag, GSM8K, and ARC.

Characterized the accuracy-efficiency trade-off: ~7% accuracy drop and +6.3 perplexity increase post-compression; studied how quantization and weight sparsity affect model behavior as performance tuning levers for LLM deployment.

projects.name: Parallel Ray Tracer with MPI Task Scheduling
bullets: Implemented and benchmarked four parallel work distribution strategies (static strip/block/cyclic, dynamic task queue) for rendering 5000×5000 pixel scenes using MPI; characterized trade-offs in throughput, load balance, and scalability across each strategy.

Achieved up to 30× speedup with static strip partitioning (55 processes); demonstrated dynamic task queue outperformed all static strategies under unpredictable workloads — identifying load imbalance as the primary bottleneck.
